name: Ema Datshi
ingredients:
120g Fresh Green Chillies
32g Spring Onions
140g Farm Cheese
25ml Vegetable Oil
6g Salt
40ml Water
instructions:
1. Rinse the chillies, onion or spring onion. Cut the chillies in half lengthwise. Remove some seeds for less heat if desired. Chop spring onion into thin slices.
2. Add all ingredients into a pot with quarter cup of water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat until chillies are cooked.
3. Add butter (optional) and cheese cubes by placing on top of other ingredients.
4. Cover the pot and simmer until cheese has melted.
5. Remove lid and stir until combined. Check salt.
6. Serve hot with red rice.

name: Shamu Datshi
ingredients:
85g Mushroom (Shitake)
30g Fresh Green Chilli
40g Cheese
25ml Vegetable Oil
5g Salt
300ml Water
instructions:
1. Rinse mushrooms and green chillies. Ensure water is completely squeezed from mushrooms.
2. Cut mushrooms in half (big ones cut again into half). Cut green chillies into half lengthwise.
3. Transfer all cut mushrooms, green chillies, water, oil and salt into a pot.
4. Cover and cook on high heat until mushrooms are half cooked.
5. Add cheese, cover again and cook until cheese begins to melt.
6. Without mixing, turn off heat and let sit for 2-3 minutes.
7. Finally mix well, check salt. Garnish with coriander leaves.
image_credit: Bhutan eCookbook, Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources

name: Phagsha Paa
ingredients:
290g Pork fillet (cut into strips)
260g Onions
270g Tomatoes
250g Fresh Green Chillies
1 tsp Chilli powder
1/4 cup Vegetable Oil
2 tsp Salt
500ml Water
instructions:
1. Wash pork fillet and cut into strips. Chop onion, tomatoes and green chillies into quarters.
2. Add pork strips, onion, tomato, pinch of salt and water into pressure cooker.
3. Cook under pressure until cooker whistles 10 times. Turn off heat and release pressure.
4. Continue cooking with lid open and wet fry pork in its own oil until tender.
5. Throw in garlic, green chillies and chilli powder (optional). Simmer over low heat until green chillies wilt.
6. Add handful of coriander leaves on top. Serve with rice.
